title: The Last Walk to the Far Beach

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: An elder wants to walk to the far beach once more, though it is a long way: go with them, or offer to carry the food.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When (subject) was young, (subject.he/she) used to walk to the far beach every season. It has been many years. (subject.His/her) legs aren't what they were, and (subject.he/she) walks slowly and steadily now. Today (subject.he/she) has told (friend) that (subject.he/she) would like to go there once more. It's a long way. (subject) knows that perfectly well.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They set off at dawn and walk at (subject)'s pace, which means many rests and a great deal of looking at things. It takes them two days. When they finally reach the far beach, (subject) sits on the sand with (subject.his/her) feet in the water for a whole afternoon, saying almost nothing. On the way home, (subject.he/she) says it was exactly the same, and completely different.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "I'll come," says (friend), "and I'll carry the food. You carry yourself." (subject) laughs. "Done." The walk is slow and hard, and halfway there (subject) has to admit (subject.he/she) needs a whole day's rest. They take it. They reach the beach a day late. Nobody minds. The sea was waiting.
